description: This line plot illustrates the similarity scores across different model layers for four language pair combinations in a multilingual large language model, as analyzed in the paper “Less, but Better: Efficient Multilingual Expansion for LLMs via Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts.” The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” ranges from 0 to 22 with integer tick marks at every 2 units, representing the depth of the model’s layers. The y-axis, labeled “Similarity,” is scaled linearly from 0.00 to 0.45 in increments of 0.05, indicating the degree of similarity (likely between representations or attention patterns) for each language pair. Four distinct lines are plotted: a solid red line (labeled with a grayed-out entry in the legend), a solid blue line labeled “en&es,” a solid green line labeled “en&el,” and a solid magenta line labeled “en&bn.” The red line starts at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, peaks around 0.26 at layer 6, dips to ~0.15 at layer 8, and then rises sharply after layer 20, reaching ~0.44 at layer 23. The blue line follows a similar trend, peaking at ~0.24 at layer 6 and ending at ~0.27 at layer 23. The green line peaks at ~0.15 at layer 6 and ends at ~0.30 at layer 23. The magenta line peaks at ~0.14 at layer 6 and ends at ~0.30 at layer 23. All lines show a general dip between layers 16 and 20 before a steep increase in the final layers, suggesting a late-stage convergence or alignment in representation similarity.
